papers.title_en: Signal or Noise? Understanding Generative Models for Real-World Sensor Time Series
papers.authors: Zitao Shuai, Zongzhe Xu, Yuntian Wu, Sirui Li, Tianhong Li, Yuzhe Yang
papers.evidence: 生成模型用于真实世界传感器时间序列，可应用于环境传感器数据
papers.tldr: 现实世界传感器时间序列的生成模型研究零散，缺乏系统理解。本文提出SensorGen大型研究，涵盖14个设置、4领域、7数据集、12信号模态，系统评估5类生成模型。关键发现：flow-matching整体性能最优；人口协变量提升纵向生成，时频建模改善高频信号；生成数据质量随规模提升，并有效增强下游任务性能。SensorGen为传感器数据生成的设计选择、评估协议和失败模式建立了广泛理解。
papers.abstract_en: Generative models have changed how machine learning represents complex data distributions, especially in language and vision, yet many real-world systems are observed instead as continuous, high-dimensional, and noisy sensor time series. Existing generative modeling of sensor data, however, remains fragmented across modalities, datasets, and task formulations, limiting a systematic understanding of when, how, and why generative models succeed or fail in real-world settings. To address this gap, we introduce SensorGen, a large-scale study of sensor-signal generation spanning 14 settings across 4 domains, 7 datasets, and 12 signal modalities. Leveraging SensorGen, we systematically evaluate generative models from five major families and uncover three key findings: (1) flow-matching models provide strong overall performance across most settings; (2) signal properties matter, with demographic covariates improving longitudinal generation and time-frequency modeling improving high-frequency signal generation; and (3) generated signals have practical utility beyond visual realism, with scaling improving generation quality and synthetic data improving downstream performance. Together, SensorGen establishes a broader understanding of design choices, evaluation protocols, and failure modes in real-world sensor data generation.

papers.title_en: Enhancing the Forecasting Capability of Multi-Model Blending Algorithms for Extreme Precipitation via Joint Use of Station and Gridded Observations
papers.authors: Yu Wang, Yong Cao, Kan Dai, Yue Shen, Xiaoqing Zeng, Ruixia Zhao
papers.evidence: 使用U-Net进行环境预测的深度学习方法
papers.tldr: 传统多模型融合算法在极端降水预报中存在极值平滑和面积扩张问题。本文提出一种U-Net两阶段框架，先进行概率分类再重建数值，并引入全国2411个气象站观测与格点数据联合监督损失函数。在2025年汛期独立样本中，对暴雨（≥50mm）的TS评分较最优NWP提升38.4%，对极端事件（≥100mm）TS提升至0.1以上，有效校正系统性雨带位移。证明了多源联合监督在提升极端降水捕捉能力方面的有效性。
papers.abstract_en: Accurate extreme precipitation forecasting is critical for disaster mitigation but remains challenging for numerical weather prediction (NWP) models due to systemic intensity underestimation and spatial displacement. Traditional precipitation multi-model blending algorithms perform pixel-by-pixel blending on the forecast field based on weights, which may lead to the expansion of precipitation areas and the smoothing of extreme values. This study proposes an U-Net based two-stage framework: probability classification followed by value reconstruction, to blend forecasts from six major NWP models. A novel station-grid joint supervision mechanism is introduced by integrating observations from 2411 national meteorological stations in China into the loss function, simultaneously constraining spatial structures and peak intensities. Evaluations using independent samples from the 2025 flood season demonstrate that our model significantly outperforms both individual NWPs and current operational products. For rainstorms (>=50 mm), the Threat Score (TS) improved by 38.4% compared to the best NWP. Notably, for extreme events (>=100 mm) driven by extratropical cyclones and the subtropical high, the model successfully elevated the TS to above 0.1, transforming forecasts from having negligible reference value into those with certain operational utility. Furthermore, the model exhibits data-driven spatial correction capabilities, effectively realigning systematic rainbelt displacements with actual precipitation centers. The inclusion of station observations specifically enhanced the TS for rainstorms by 10.4% and effectively balanced the Bias. These results highlight the efficacy of multi-source joint supervision in enhancing the capture of extreme precipitation events.

papers.title_en: Physics-guided spatiotemporal neural models for fuel density prediction
papers.authors: Tolga Caglar, Jaynil Jaiswal, Saqib Azim, Yudhir Gala, Mai H. Nguyen, Ilkay Altintas
papers.evidence: 提出物理引导的时空深度学习架构（ConvLSTM、AFNONet、ViViT），可迁移至空气质量预测
papers.tldr: 野火燃料密度预测中，纯数据驱动模型缺乏物理约束导致精度和稳定性不足。本文提出物理引导机器学习框架，通过将质量守恒和蔓延速率等可微物理损失项融入ConvLSTM、自适应傅里叶神经算子和视频视觉Transformer等深度模型，实现了物理约束与数据学习的结合。实验表明，该方法在多项独立试验中预测精度和稳定性均优于无物理约束的基线，为高效物理可信的火势预报提供了新途径。
papers.abstract_en: This paper presents a physics-guided machine learning (PGML) framework for fuel density prediction, integrating physics constraints and domain knowledge into deep learning models to enhance model accuracy and stability. We explore three deep learning architectures -- ConvLSTM, Adaptive Fourier Neural Operator (AFNONet), and Video Vision Transformer (ViViT) -- to model the spatiotemporal evolution of fuel density. Our approach incorporates differentiable physics-informed terms in the loss function, including a mass-conserving fuel transport term and a rate-of-spread estimation. Experimental results, averaged across multiple independent trials, demonstrate that the proposed PGML framework outperforms purely data-driven baselines without physics constraints in both accuracy and stability. This framework enables computationally efficient, physically plausible fire forecasting to support adaptive prescribed burn management.
